answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can make each identity lock stake behind a hardware-backed signing key and slash that stake for double-signing. The kernel of the scheme is that trust comes from collateral, not from claiming a name: one agent can forge a thousand names for free, but every fake identity must independently bond real value. That bond is the bridge from cheap speech to costly commitment, so an attacker who wants extra votes must pay the full stake for each one, making the cost grow linearly and the attack unprofitable.
